column1: # Pokémon Violet 4.0.0 (v786432), Game Freak Trinity, SDK 13.3.13, NVN.
# Experimental Android bring-up on AYN Odin 2 / Adreno 740 (2026-11-18).
# Shader tables come from this build's own main and Trinity packs; they differ from Scarlet's in a few keys.
# The host supplies the movie API; main takes nothing else from subsdk0.
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource. nninitStartup reserves a 12 GB
# StandardAllocator region; the survey's 4.375 GB alias region refused it and
# boot aborted in the Oodle decoder. A 14.375 GB alias region in a 15 GB block boots.
# Same engine as Scarlet (0100A3D008C5C000): without the pool enforced the allocators count the 12 GB setup pages twice,
# the periodic free-memory sample wraps to 0, and the wild Pokémon spawner despawns every wild Pokémon.
# Without patches.py the game asks for present interval 2 and runs at 30 (as on the Switch), whatever DM_FPS_PIN holds.
# patches.py (the community dynamic-FPS cut, as Scarlet's) makes it ask for interval 1 and step by the time that really passed;
# fps_ceiling 30 holds it at 30 by default and porter's --fps60 lifts the ceiling (DM_FPS_CEILING=0).
# Measured on the Odin 2 in Poco Path (one run): turning the camera for 2 s at 33 fps (DM_FPS_PIN=40) and back for 2 s pinned at 30 returned to the same view
# within about 1 degree, either order; frame counting would have missed by about 18. Below 30 fps (CPU load, about 15 fps) a turn came up short, so the
# game slows down there rather than skipping ahead, as on the Switch. The overworld's frame work is 25 to 32 ms here, so --fps60 gives about 33 fps, not 60
# 35,937 shaders, including BNSH inside Oodle-compressed arc/data.trpfs entries.
